instantiated_cells.justification: Section 13.66 requires that, except as exempted under §13.621, no person may engage in lobbying as a lobbyist unless licensed under §13.63 and authorized under §13.65, meaning all paid lobbyists must register/be licensed.
Section 13.63(1)(a) states that a lobbyist license "shall expire on December 31 of each even-numbered year," establishing a biennial (24-month) renewal cycle.

While §13.695(2) requires agency-side reporting of changes within 10 days, §13.64(3) similarly requires written notice "before" attempting to influence action in any new general area, and the closest specified time frame for change notifications in the bundle is 10 days.

Section 13.66 prohibits any person from engaging in lobbying as a lobbyist unless already licensed under §13.63 and authorized under §13.65; the lobbyist must be licensed BEFORE lobbying, i.e., 0 days after first lobbying activity (no post-activity grace period).

Lobbyists file a license application under §13.63(1)(a), principals file a separate registration statement under §13.64(1), and a separate written authorization linking the two is filed under §13.65 — i.e., separate filings by each party rather than a single combined form.
Section 13.63(1)(a) enumerates the required application contents (social security number, signature, fee) and makes no reference to a photograph submission requirement.

Section 13.621(3) exempts elective state officials, local officials, tribal officials, and legislative employees acting in official capacity from §§13.63, 13.64, 13.65, 13.68, and 13.695; §13.621(2) exempts agencies (and named officials) that file under §13.695 from most lobbying-law sections.

Section 13.621(2) provides that agencies filing the statement under §13.695 (and officials named therein) are not subject to §§13.625, 13.63, 13.64, 13.65, or 13.68 except as provided in §13.695, creating a partial exemption with a separate, lighter reporting regime for state agencies.
